question: Explain operating leverage and financial leverage. How are they related to business risk and financial risk?
sources: Leverage analysis: operating, financial and combined leverage

points.label: Operating leverage
points.description: Operating leverage arises from fixed operating costs; because of them a change in sales causes a larger percentage change in EBIT.

points.label: Measure of operating leverage
points.description: Degree of operating leverage = percentage change in EBIT / percentage change in sales, or contribution / EBIT. Higher operating leverage means higher business risk.

points.label: Financial leverage
points.description: Financial leverage arises from fixed financial charges such as interest on debt (and preference dividend); a change in EBIT causes a larger percentage change in EPS.

points.label: Measure of financial leverage
points.description: Degree of financial leverage = percentage change in EPS / percentage change in EBIT, or EBIT / EBT. Higher financial leverage means higher financial risk.

points.label: Combined leverage
points.description: Combined leverage = operating leverage x financial leverage; it shows the total risk and the effect of a change in sales on EPS.
